key_insight: Leveraging generative modeling directly in pixel space enables a monocular depth foundation model (Pixel-Perfect Depth, PPD) to produce high-fidelity, flying-pixel–free depth maps and point clouds that retain fine geometric details lost by prior models.
problem_solved: Existing geometry foundation models produce flying pixels and blur or lose fine structural details in depth/point-cloud outputs, limiting accuracy for robotics, SLAM, and AR—this work removes those artifacts and restores pixel-level geometric fidelity.
method: Introduce Pixel-Perfect Depth (PPD): a monocular depth foundation model built on generative modeling in pixel space to learn pixel-level priors for geometry.
Predicts high-quality depth maps and converts them to point clouds while using the generative pixel prior to suppress flying pixels and reconstruct fine details.
End-to-end design that fuses image-conditioned generation with geometric output constraints to produce stable, artifact-free 3D geometry.
impact: Provides practitioners a way to get cleaner, more accurate 3D reconstructions from images, improving downstream tasks such as visual SLAM, robot navigation, and AR content placement by reducing artifact-driven failures and preserving detailed geometry.
visual_elements: Before/after side-by-side: input image, baseline depth, PPD depth, rendered point-cloud — highlights removal of flying pixels and detail recovery.
Pipeline diagram: image → pixel-space generative module → depth map → point cloud, annotated with the role of the pixel prior.
Zoomed-in detail comparisons: close-ups showing preserved thin structures (edges, wires, small objects) and quantitative error overlays (heatmaps).
Bar/line chart: metrics comparison (e.g., flying-pixel rate, depth RMSE, detail-preservation score) across baselines and PPD.
paper_authors: Gangwei Xu, Haotong Lin, Hongcheng Luo, Haiyang Sun, Bing Wang
